title: Three of 12 bullets police fired into attacker were fatal
article: Three of the dozen bullets fired into a knife-wielding attacker by two junior Vancouver police officers would have killed him on their own, a coroner's inquest was told yesterday.

Gerald Chenery was shot 12 times and grazed by one bullet during a confrontation in a Downtown Eastside alley with two rookie officers who had graduated from police training just weeks before the Boxing Day 2004 shooting, testified forensic pathologist Dr. Charles Lee.
Nine bullets were removed from Chenery's body including one lodged in his spinal bone, said Lee.
The three deadly shots were fired into the 29-year-old's back by Const. Bryan Smith, 31, as Chenery stabbed and flailed at Const. Elizabeth Clark, 37.

The two officers -- Smith had six weeks on the job and Clark eight weeks -- have testified they felt they had no choice but to shoot Chenery, who was wanted on a warrant for breaching parole after getting out of federal jail three days earlier. He had spent the previous seven years in jail on various sentences.
Clark fired four shots, hitting Chenery once in the groin and missing him three times, while Smith pumped 11 shots into him.
Smith had testified earlier he kept shooting because the bullets seemed to have no effect on Chenery.
Lee said it's unpredictable how someone will react to being shot.
"Some people who are just grazed will fall down," he said. "Some will ignore pain. They don't realize they're been shot."
The autopsy revealed a "pretty low amount" of cocaine in Chenery's system that had already been metabolized, said Lee.

Sgt. Roy Bertolo, who was the first backup police officer to arrive, testified he saw Chenery sprinting down the lane, stopping and screaming an obscenity and sprinting back to where the officers were before charging at Clark.
Still in his vehicle, Bertolo said he ducked when he saw the gunfire flashes and heard the bullets hitting his car.
"I knew I was in the crossfire and, at that point, I put my head down," he testified.
"I feared I was going to get shot in the head or facial area."
One of the bullets lodged in the rubber stripping just below the passenger door window, cracking the glass.
